problem: Suppose that $f(x,y)=(x+1)^{2}(y+2).$ Which of the following shaded areas gives the solution to the inequality $f(x,y)\le 0?$

feedback.problem: Suppose that $f(x,y)=(x-2)^{3}(y+3).$ Which of the following shaded areas gives the solution to the inequality $f(x,y)>0?$
feedback.worked_solution:
Notice that $f(x,y)$ equals zero when $x=2$ and $y=-3.$ These lines divide the $xy$-plane into four regions, as shown below. Since we have a strict inequality, we use dashed lines to divide the plane.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14041262/assets/6c1830847adf66b3d015227fb2b822d236cc0ca04d4e79b34485e0e307bebfb2.png)

To determine the sign of $f(x,y)$ in each region, we pick four test points, one for each region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14041262/assets/e04638efe40ea1813185855bb8c9a47e3e782487f6497ba63c7ed5e9046af421.png)

Next, we calculate the sign of $f(x,y)$ in each region using a sign table:

|  | Test point | $(x-2)^{3}$ | $(y+3)$ | $f(x,y)$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Top-Left | $(1,-2)$ | $-$ | $+$ | $-$ |
| Top-Right | $(3,-2)$ | $+$ | $+$ | $+$ |
| Bottom-Left | $(1,-4)$ | $-$ | $-$ | $+$ |
| Bottom-Right | $(3,-4)$ | $+$ | $-$ | $-$ |

 

Finally, on our diagram, we shade in the solutions to $f(x,y)>0$ using the *last* column of the table above.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14041262/assets/51df420aa99597c5f476be571557aa9f1c91a1ec1f888687058bfd0fe96813e4.png)
